Below is a practical taxonomy of **grid-based logic games**, with your listed titles grouped by their **primary solving mechanic**.

---

# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## 1. Shading / Painting Puzzles
Core action: decide which cells are black/shaded vs white/unshaded.

### 1.1 Visibility / illumination shading
- **Akari** — place lights in white cells; illumination constraints determine valid placements.
- **Kurodoko** — shade cells so numbered white cells “see” the required count.
- **Kurotto** — shade cells around circles according to summed runs of black cells.

### 1.2 Connectivity + forbidden patterns shading
- **Heyawake** — shade cells by room counts, no adjacent blacks, white connectivity, room-span rule.
- **Hitori** — shade duplicate numbers while keeping black cells non-adjacent and whites connected.
- **Nurikabe** — shade to separate numbered white islands; black cells form one connected wall with no 2×2.
- **Usowan** — shade cells with local counts, one false clue per room, no adjacent blacks, white connectivity.
- **Yajilin** — shade some cells according to arrow clues while drawing a loop through the rest.
- **Nuritwin** — shade paired equal-sized blocks in each region; all shaded cells globally connected.
- **Norinori** — shade cells in dominoes; each region contains exactly two shaded cells.

### 1.3 Shape-constrained shading
- **Choco Banana** — black connected components must be rectangles/squares; white components must not be.
- **LITS** — shade one tetromino per region; shaded cells connected; no touching same tetromino types; no 2×2.
- **Shakashaka** — place triangular half-cell shadings so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares.
- **Tilepaint** — color whole regions subject to row/column count clues from diagonal cells.
- **Sto-stone** — shade cells in rooms with gravity/drop behavior constraints.

### 1.4 Path/maze by shading
- **Nurimeizu** — shade whole rooms to create a maze/path from S to G with shortest-path marker constraints.
- **Nurimisaki** — shade cells so circled white cells become “promontories”; white connected, no 2×2 of either color.

---

## 2. Loop-Drawing Puzzles
Core action: draw a single closed loop on or through the grid.

### 2.1 Edge-based loop puzzles
- **Slitherlink** — draw a loop along grid edges matching numeric edge counts.
- **Masyu** — draw a loop through pearl cells with straight/turn behavior rules.
- **Mid-loop** — draw a loop so black circles are midpoints of straight segments.

### 2.2 Cell-center loop puzzles
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop passes through cells; white circles in a region are all straight or all turning.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop visits each room once and uses either all moons or all suns in a room, alternating type by room.
- **Nagareru** — directional loop with arrow cells and wind constraints.
- **Suraromu** — loop must pass gates in numbered order constraints.
- **Yajilin** — hybrid: loop through unshaded cells plus shading clues.

---

## 3. Path / Connection Puzzles (non-loop)
Core action: connect endpoints or route paths, but not necessarily as a single loop.

### 3.1 Pair-connection paths
- **Numberlink** — connect matching numbers with non-crossing paths.

### 3.2 Directed or object-emission paths
- **Pencils** — identify pencil shapes and draw a line from each tip with length constraints.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas by straight arrows; sums in gray areas must match.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles across countries by exact distances without crossing tracks.

### 3.3 Network connection
- **Hashiwokakero** — connect numbered islands with bridges into one connected network.

---

## 4. Region Division / Partition Puzzles
Core action: divide the grid into regions or blocks satisfying clues.

### 4.1 Rectangle partition
- **Shikaku** — partition into rectangles, each containing one clue equal to area.

### 4.2 Polyform / shape partition
- **Sashigane** — partition into one-cell-wide L-shapes with circle/arrow clues.
- **Five Cells** — partition into regions of exactly five cells with border-count clues.
- **Double Choco** — partition into blocks each containing matching white/gray shapes.
- **Chained Block** — determine black-cell blocks with size/shape uniqueness within corner-touching chains.

---

## 5. Region Filling / Number Placement Puzzles
Core action: fill cells with numbers under region and adjacency constraints.

### 5.1 Latin / room-based number placement
- **Sudoku** — classic 1–9 row/column/box placement.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with 1..n; arrow clues indicate local maxima; equal numbers cannot touch across rooms.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers; equal numbers in row/column must be sufficiently separated.

### 5.2 Polyomino-size number filling
- **Fillomino** — partition into same-number regions whose size equals the number.

### 5.3 Number placement from word/list packing
- **Nansuke** — place given numbers into slots in the grid.

### 5.4 Binary-orientation symbol filling
- **Juosan** — fill each cell with horizontal or vertical marks under territory balance and run-length constraints.

---

## 6. Object Placement Puzzles
Core action: place discrete objects/symbols into cells.

### 6.1 Light / marker placement
- **Akari** — place bulbs.
- **Evolomino** — place squares to form evolving blocks along arrows.

### 6.2 Sequential object placement
- **Hebi** — place snake numbers 1–5 in chains with visibility and non-touching constraints.

---

## 7. Hybrid Puzzles
Games that strongly combine two major mechanics.

- **Yajilin** — shading + loop.
- **Nurimeizu** — shading + maze/path.
- **Pencils** — shape identification + path drawing.
- **Satogaeri** — movement + region occupancy.
- **Yosenabe** — movement/path + arithmetic region sums.
- **Double Choco** — partition + shape matching.
- **Evolomino** — placement + polyform growth logic.
- **Sto-stone** — shading + gravity simulation.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop + room visitation logic.
- **Dotchi-Loop** — loop + region pattern consistency.

---

# Alternative high-level taxonomy by solver experience

If you want a more user-facing taxonomy, these games can also be grouped as:

- **Shade cells:** Heyawake, Hitori, Nurikabe, Kurodoko, LITS, Norinori, etc.
- **Draw a loop:** Slitherlink, Masyu, Mid-loop, Dotchi-Loop, Moon-or-Sun, Nagareru, Suraromu, Yajilin.
- **Connect things:** Numberlink, Hashiwokakero.
- **Divide into regions:** Shikaku, Sashigane, Five Cells, Double Choco, Chained Block.
- **Fill numbers/symbols:** Sudoku, Fillomino, Makaro, Ripple Effect, Nansuke, Juosan.
- **Move/place objects:** Akari, Hebi, Evolomino, Pencils, Satogaeri, Yosenabe.
- **Hybrids / unusual mechanics:** Nurimeizu, Sto-stone, Shakashaka.
